title: Clean and oil the air filter
entry_state: Bike cool, on a stand.
exit_state: Clean, evenly oiled filter sealed in the airbox, cover or seat refitted, service recorded.
completeness: Covers getting into the airbox, filter removal, intake check, washing, oiling, greasing the seal and refitting.

required_tools.name: Foam filter cleaner or warm soapy water

required_parts.name: Spare foam filter
required_parts.purpose: Fit if the old one is torn, hard or shrunken.

critical_stop_conditions: Torn, hardened or shrunken foam: do not refit it.
Filter lip not sealing all the way round: do not start the engine.
Never clean the filter with gasoline or a low flash-point solvent.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Clean the air filter after each race (or 2.5 hours), straight away after riding in rain or mud, and more often in dust. Write down the date, the hours and how dirty the filter was last time.

steps.title: Support the bike
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright on a stand on firm, level ground so it cannot tip while you work.

steps.title: Open the airbox
steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolt and the left side cover bolt. Ease the rear of the left side cover outward, pull it forward to free its hooks and lift it away.

steps.title: Take the filter out
steps.instruction: Undo the wing bolt and lift the filter out with its frame. Look into the intake duct and the throttle body. Dirt past the filter means it was not sealing.

branches.label: Dirt past the filter
branches.condition: Dust or grit on the clean side: clean the duct and throttle body thoroughly before going on, and check the seal extra carefully on refit.

steps.title: Block the intake
steps.instruction: Stuff a clean, lint-free towel into the throttle body opening, then wipe the inside of the airbox with a clean damp towel. No dirt may fall into the intake.

steps.title: Free the foam
steps.instruction: Slide the foam off its frame.

steps.title: Wash the foam
steps.instruction: Wash the foam in a high flash-point solvent or hot soapy water, rinse it in clear water until no cleaner is left, then squeeze it dry in a clean towel. Never twist, wring or blow it dry: the foam tears easily.

branches.label: Foam damaged
branches.condition: Any tear, hardening or shrinkage: fit a new filter instead and note it in the record.

steps.title: Oil the foam
steps.instruction: Let the foam dry completely. Soak it in good foam filter oil and work it in so every part is evenly coated. Squeeze out the excess without wringing; slightly too much oil is better than too little. Pat the inside with a paper towel to lift off any pooled oil.

steps.title: Grease the sealing faces
steps.instruction: Spread grease on all the mating surfaces and the wing bolt hole in the airbox and intake tract.

steps.title: Put the foam on its frame
steps.instruction: Fit the foam back on its frame with the pins on the frame lined up with the holes in the foam. Coat the filter lip and the lip seat in the airbox with a thick layer of all-purpose grease so it seals all the way round.
verification: Foam on its frame, lip greased.

steps.title: Take the towel out
steps.instruction: Pull the towel out of the throttle body. Never close the airbox with it inside.

steps.title: Fit the filter
steps.instruction: Put the filter in so the guide blade on the holder lines up with the projection in the airbox and the open side of the guide blade faces outward. Tighten the wing bolt. Run a finger round the edge: the lip must sit flat everywhere.
verification: Filter seated and secured, lip flat all round.

steps.title: Close up
steps.instruction: Hook the left side cover onto the ribs of the radiator shroud and airbox and push its tab into the slot in the rear fender. Refit the side cover bolt (7.0 N·m (62 in·lb)) and the seat bolt (25 N·m (18 ft·lb)).

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, filter condition, whether the clean side was dirty and whether a new filter went in.

title: Change the engine oil and filter
entry_state: Engine warm, bike upright on a stand on level ground.
exit_state: Fresh oil at the correct level, new filter fitted, no leaks, change recorded.
completeness: Covers draining, filter replacement, refilling to the correct amount and the level check through the inspection window.

required_parts.name: Engine oil
required_parts.purpose: SAE 10W-40, rated API SG, SH, SJ, SL or SM with JASO MA, MA1 or MA2.

required_parts.name: Oil filter
required_parts.purpose: New filter at every filter change.

required_parts.name: Drain bolt gasket
required_parts.purpose: Fit a new one every time.

required_parts.name: Oil filter cap O-ring
required_parts.purpose: Fit a new one every time.

prerequisites: Engine warmed up so the oil carries the dirt out.
critical_stop_conditions: Never fit the filter inside out: it blocks the oil flow and seizes the engine.
No oil visible in the window after refilling: stop and find out why before riding.
Do not race the engine before the oil has reached every part.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Change the engine oil every 6 races (or 15 hours) and the oil filter every 6 races (or 15 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Warm the oil
steps.instruction: Run the engine until it is thoroughly warm, then stop it. Warm oil drains faster and carries the dirt with it.

steps.title: Open the filler
steps.instruction: With the bike upright on its stand, put a drain pan under the engine and remove the oil filler plug.

steps.title: Drain the oil
steps.instruction: Remove the oil drain bolt and keep the bike upright so all the oil can run out. Look at the oil and the bolt for metal flakes.

branches.label: Metal in the oil
branches.condition: Large flakes or chunks on the bolt or in the oil: do not refill and ride; have the engine inspected and note it in the record.

steps.title: Take out the old filter
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cap bolts and take off the cap with its O-ring and spring. Pull out the old filter and wipe the housing clean.

steps.title: Fit the new filter
steps.instruction: Put grease on the grommet of the new filter and fit it with the grommet facing the engine. Inside out stops the oil flow.
verification: Filter in, grommet toward the engine.

steps.title: Refit the filter cap
steps.instruction: Fit a new O-ring to the cap with a little grease, fit the spring, and refit the cap and its bolts. Tighten the bolts to 12 N·m (106 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the drain bolt
steps.instruction: Once the oil has stopped dripping, fit the drain bolt with a new gasket. Tighten it to 10 N·m (89 in·lb).
verification: Drain bolt in with new gasket.

steps.title: Refill
steps.instruction: With the filter changed, pour in 0.9 L (1.0 US qt) of SAE 10W-40 oil rated API SG, SH, SJ, SL or SM with JASO MA, MA1 or MA2. If you changed only the oil, use 0.8 L (0.8 US qt). The 1.0 L (1.1 US qt) figure is for a completely dry engine after a rebuild. Fill slowly through the filler opening and stop at the high level line.

steps.title: Close the filler
steps.instruction: Refit the oil filler plug. Tighten it to 3.5 N·m (31 in·lb).

steps.title: Check the level
steps.instruction: Start the engine and let it idle for a few minutes, without revving. Stop it, wait a few minutes for the oil to settle, then hold the bike upright and look at the inspection window low on the right side of the engine. The level must sit between the high and low lines. Too high: draw some out with a syringe. Too low: add the same oil through the filler.

branches.label: No oil in the window
branches.condition: No oil showing even with the bike tipped slightly right: drain the engine and refill with the full amount.

steps.title: Check for leaks
steps.instruction: Look round the drain bolt and the filter cap for any leak.

steps.title: Record the change
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used, amount and whether the filter was changed.

entry_state: Engine completely cold, bike upright.
exit_state: Coolant at the bottom of the filler neck, air bled out, no leaks, recorded.

required_parts.name: Coolant
required_parts.purpose: Permanent ethylene-glycol antifreeze made for aluminium engines and radiators, mixed half and half with soft or distilled water.

required_parts.name: Drain bolt gasket
required_parts.purpose: Fit a new one every time the bolt comes out.

required_parts.name: Air bleeder screw O-ring
required_parts.purpose: Fit a new one when the bleeder is opened.

prerequisites: Engine cold. Never open the radiator cap on a hot engine: steam and coolant can burst out.
critical_stop_conditions: White cotton-like flakes in the old coolant mean aluminium corrosion: flush the system.
Brown coolant means rust: flush the system.
Coolant on the tyres makes them slippery: wash any spill off at once.
Never use hard tap water: it scales the passages.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the coolant level after each race (or 2.5 hours) and the water hoses after each race (or 2.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Stand the bike upright
steps.instruction: Hold or stand the bike so the radiator cap is level and highest, so any trapped air can rise to it.

steps.title: Open the radiator cap in two stages
steps.instruction: Turn the cap counterclockwise to the first stop and wait a few seconds. Then push down, turn it further and lift it off.

steps.title: Read the level
steps.instruction: With the engine cold, the coolant must reach the bottom of the filler neck. Check the hoses for cracks and loose clamps and the radiator fins for mud; wash the fins with a gentle stream, never a pressure washer.

branches.label: Level low, coolant still clean
branches.condition: Top up to the bottom of the filler neck with the same mix, look for the leak that lowered it, then refit the cap.

branches.label: Coolant due or dirty
branches.condition: Change the coolant.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: Put a drain pan under the coolant drain bolt on the water pump cover and remove the bolt. Let the system empty. Look at the old coolant.

branches.label: Flakes or brown coolant
branches.condition: Whitish flakes or brown coolant: the system must be flushed before refilling. Record it.

steps.title: Refit the drain bolt
steps.instruction: Check the system for damage and loose joints, then fit the drain bolt with a new gasket.
verification: Drain bolt in with new gasket.

steps.title: Fill slowly
steps.instruction: Pour coolant in slowly up to the bottom of the filler neck so the air can escape as it fills.

steps.title: Bleed the air
steps.instruction: Lean the bike slightly so the filler neck is level and uppermost. Loosen the air bleeder screw on top of the radiator until coolant starts to come out, fit a new O-ring to the screw and tighten it. Tighten it to 1.6 N·m (14 in·lb).
verification: Coolant ran from the bleeder, screw tight.

steps.title: Top up and close
steps.instruction: Top up to the bottom of the filler neck again and fit the radiator cap. Check for leaks.

steps.title: Warm up and recheck
steps.instruction: Start the engine, warm it up thoroughly and stop it. When it is completely cold again, open the cap in two stages and top up to the bottom of the filler neck if needed.

steps.title: Refit the cap
steps.instruction: Fit the radiator cap fully and check round the hoses and drain bolt for leaks.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down what you did, the condition of the old coolant and any leak you found.

entry_state: Engine cold, bike on a stand.
exit_state: Correct plug fitted at the right gap and torque, tank and bodywork back on, recorded.

required_parts.name: Spark plug NGK CPR8EB-9
required_parts.purpose: Replacement plug.

prerequisites: No smoking, flames or sparks: the fuel system is opened.
critical_stop_conditions: Fuel hose joint not clicked and locked: do not start the engine.
Plug will not start by hand: stop and check the thread rather than forcing it.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Inspect the spark plug after each race (or 2.5 hours) and fit a new one every 3 races (or 7.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Let the engine cool
steps.instruction: Work on a cold engine, in a well-ventilated place with no flames or sparks nearby: the fuel tank has to come off.

steps.title: Take off the seat and covers
steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolts and side cover bolts, unhook both side covers, then lift the rear of the seat and slide it rearward off the bike.
verification: Seat and covers off and stored together with their bolts.

steps.title: Remove the radiator shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the radiator shroud bolts and lift off the shroud on each side.

steps.title: Disconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Unhook the tank band and remove the fuel tank bolt. Wrap a clean rag round the fuel hose joint and brush any dirt off the joint first. verification: Seat and covers off and stored together with their bolts.

steps.title: Remove the radiator shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the radiator shroud bolts and lift off the shroud on each side.

steps.title: Disconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Unhook the tank band and remove the fuel tank bolt. Wrap a clean rag round the fuel hose joint and brush any dirt off the joint first. Put a flat screwdriver in the slit of the joint lock, turn it to release the lock and pull the hose joint off the outlet pipe: a little fuel under pressure will come out. Cover the pipe and the hose joint with clean plastic bags. Open the clamps and unplug the fuel pump connector.
verification: Fuel joint off and bagged, pump connector unplugged, spilled fuel wiped up.

branches.label: Fuel keeps running
branches.condition: Fuel keeps pouring from the hose or pipe: stop, make sure nothing can ignite it, wipe it up and let it settle before going on.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Lift the fuel tank straight up and away and set it somewhere it cannot be knocked over.

steps.title: Clean round the plug
steps.instruction: Blow or brush the dirt away from round the plug cap hole in the cylinder head cover so nothing can fall into the cylinder.

steps.title: Pull off the plug cap
steps.instruction: Pull the cap straight off the plug by its body, never by the lead.

steps.title: Remove the plug
steps.instruction: Unscrew the plug with a spark plug socket and lift it out.

steps.title: Read the plug
steps.instruction: Look at the plug. Do not clean or regap this plug: if it is oily, sooty, worn, cracked or the gap is wrong, fit a new one. An oily or sooty plug also points to a running problem worth finding.

branches.label: Plug worn or damaged
branches.condition: Fit a new NGK CR9EIB-9 instead.

steps.title: Check the gap
steps.instruction: Measure the gap with a wire-type gauge. It must be 0.8 to 0.9 mm (0.031 to 0.035 in.). If it is outside this, fit a new plug.

steps.title: Fit the plug
steps.instruction: Screw the plug in by hand first so it cannot cross-thread, then tighten it to 13 N·m (115 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the plug cap
steps.instruction: Push the cap on so it lines up with the line on the cylinder head cover, then pull up lightly to make sure it has snapped on.

steps.title: Refit the tank and fuel line
steps.instruction: Check the joint lock on the fuel hose for wear or bending: a bent lock means a new fuel hose. Wipe a trace of engine oil on the outlet pipe, push the hose joint straight on until it clicks, then push the lock home until it clicks. Push and pull the joint a few times to prove it is locked. Reconnect the fuel pump connector and hold the lead in its clamps. Make sure the frame dampers are in place and the throttle cables are not trapped, then set the tank down and fit the tank bolt. Tighten the bolt to 8.0 N·m (71 in·lb). Hook the band back on.

Refit the covers you removed, slide the seat forward so its hooks go under the frame collar, and fit the seat bolts. Tighten them to 25 N·m (18 ft·lb). Pull up on the back of the seat to be sure it is held.

steps.title: Start and check
steps.instruction: Start the engine and check it runs cleanly and nothing leaks round the fuel joint.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down the plug reading, the gap and whether a new plug went in.

steps.instruction: Check the valve clearances every 6 races (or 15 hours). Write down the date and hours. The engine must be cold, at room temperature.

steps.title: Make sure the engine is cold
steps.instruction: Let the engine cool completely. Clearances measured on a warm engine are wrong.

steps.title: Take off the seat and covers
steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolts and side cover bolts, unhook both side covers, then lift the rear of the seat and slide it rearward off the bike.

steps.title: Free the plug cap
steps.instruction: Remove the plug cap retainer plate bolt and plate, then pull the spark plug cap off by its body.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder head cover
steps.instruction: Remove the head cover bolts and their washers, open the clamp if needed, and lift the cover off. Take out the head cover gasket and the spark plug hole gasket.

steps.title: Open the alternator cover
steps.instruction: Remove the two plugs or caps from the alternator cover: one shows the timing mark, the other gives access to the rotor nut.

steps.title: Set top dead centre on compression
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise with a wrench on the rotor nut until the top mark lines up with the grooves on the alternator cover. The timing marks on the camshaft sprockets must then sit almost level with the top surface of the cylinder head. If they do not, turn the crank one more full turn.

steps.title: Measure every valve
steps.instruction: Slide feeler gauges between each cam lobe and its rocker arm, for all four valves. Write down every reading.

steps.title: Compare with the standard
steps.instruction: The intake clearance must be 0.08 to 0.12 mm (0.0031 to 0.0047 in.) and the exhaust clearance 0.14 to 0.18 mm (0.0055 to 0.0071 in.).

critical_stop_conditions: A clearance out of range: do not run the engine until it has been corrected.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the valve clearances every 6 races (or 15 hours). Write down the date and hours. The engine must be cold, at room temperature.

steps.title: Make sure the engine is cold
steps.instruction: Let the engine cool completely. Clearances measured on a warm engine are wrong.

steps.title: Take off the seat and covers
steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolts and side cover bolts, unhook both side covers, then lift the rear of the seat and slide it rearward off the bike.
verification: Seat and covers off and stored together with their bolts.

steps.title: Remove the radiator shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the radiator shroud bolts and lift off the shroud on each side.

steps.title: Disconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Unhook the tank band and remove the fuel tank bolt. Wrap a clean rag round the fuel hose joint and brush any dirt off the joint first. Put a flat screwdriver in the slit of the joint lock, turn it to release the lock and pull the hose joint off the outlet pipe: a little fuel under pressure will come out. Cover the pipe and the hose joint with clean plastic bags. Open the clamps and unplug the fuel pump connector.
verification: Fuel joint off and bagged, pump connector unplugged, spilled fuel wiped up.

branches.label: Fuel keeps running
branches.condition: Fuel keeps pouring from the hose or pipe: stop, make sure nothing can ignite it, wipe it up and let it settle before going on.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Lift the fuel tank straight up and away and set it somewhere it cannot be knocked over.
verification: Tank off, no sparks or flames anywhere near.

steps.title: Free the plug cap
steps.instruction: Remove the plug cap retainer plate bolt and plate, then pull the spark plug cap off by its body.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder head cover
steps.instruction: Remove the head cover bolts and their washers, open the clamp if needed, and lift the cover off. Take out the head cover gasket and the spark plug hole gasket.

steps.title: Open the alternator cover
steps.instruction: Remove the two plugs or caps from the alternator cover: one shows the timing mark, the other gives access to the rotor nut.

steps.title: Set top dead centre on compression
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise with a wrench on the rotor nut until the top mark lines up with the grooves on the alternator cover. The timing marks on the camshaft sprockets must then sit almost level with the top surface of the cylinder head. If they do not, turn the crank one more full turn.
verification: Top mark aligned, cam marks level with the head.

steps.title: Measure every valve
steps.instruction: Slide feeler gauges between each cam lobe and its rocker arm, for all four valves. Write down every reading.

steps.title: Compare with the standard
steps.instruction: The intake clearance must be 0.08 to 0.12 mm (0.0031 to 0.0047 in.) and the exhaust clearance 0.14 to 0.18 mm (0.0055 to 0.0071 in.).

branches.label: Any valve out of range
branches.condition: Adjusting the clearance means changing shims: have a competent mechanic do it before the engine runs again, and record the readings.

steps.title: Prepare the seals
steps.instruction: Clean any oil off the liquid gasket areas with a high flash-point solvent and dry them. Fit a new spark plug hole gasket with its stepped side facing down and a new head cover gasket on the cover, with liquid gasket where the old gasket had it. Make sure the upper chain guide is bottomed against the cover, or the cam chain can lift the cover and cause a leak.
verification: New gaskets in place, chain guide bottomed.

steps.title: Refit the head cover
steps.instruction: Fit the cover, put the washers on with their metal side up and tighten the bolts to 10 N·m (89 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the alternator cover plugs
steps.instruction: Refit the two plugs or caps.

steps.title: Refit the plug cap
steps.instruction: Push the plug cap on in line with the mark on the head cover and pull up lightly to check it has snapped on. Refit the retainer plate and tighten its bolt to 10 N·m (89 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the tank and fuel line
steps.instruction: Check the joint lock on the fuel hose for wear or bending: a bent lock means a new fuel hose. Wipe a trace of engine oil on the outlet pipe, push the hose joint straight on until it clicks, then push the lock home until it clicks. Push and pull the joint a few times to prove it is locked. Reconnect the fuel pump connector and hold the lead in its clamps. Make sure the frame dampers are in place and the throttle cables are not trapped, then set the tank down and fit the tank bolt. Tighten the bolt to 8.0 N·m (71 in·lb). Hook the band back on.
verification: Fuel joint clicked and locked, connector plugged in, nothing trapped under the tank.

steps.title: Refit the shrouds and seat
steps.instruction: Fit both radiator shrouds. Tighten the shroud bolts to 7.0 N·m (62 in·lb). Refit the covers you removed, slide the seat forward so its hooks go under the frame collar, and fit the seat bolts. Tighten them to 25 N·m (18 ft·lb). Pull up on the back of the seat to be sure it is held.

steps.title: Run and check for leaks
steps.instruction: Start the engine, let it idle and look round the head cover for oil leaks.

steps.title: Record the readings
steps.instruction: Write down all four clearances and whether any valve needs adjusting.

title: Check the valve clearances
entry_state: Engine cold, bike on a stand.
exit_state: All four clearances measured and recorded, head cover resealed, tank back on.
completeness: Covers getting to the head, finding compression top dead centre, measuring all four valves and resealing the cover.

steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolts on both sides and slide the seat rearward, then take off both side covers and the radiator screen bolts.

steps.title: Remove the radiator shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the radiator shroud bolts and lift off the shroud on each side.

steps.title: Disconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Unhook the tank band and remove the fuel tank bolt. Wrap a clean rag round the fuel hose joint and brush any dirt off the joint first. Put a flat screwdriver in the slit of the joint lock, turn it to release the lock and pull the hose joint off the outlet pipe: a little fuel under pressure will come out. branches.label: Fuel keeps running
branches.condition: Fuel keeps pouring from the hose or pipe: stop, make sure nothing can ignite it, wipe it up and let it settle before going on.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Lift the fuel tank straight up and away and set it somewhere it cannot be knocked over.
verification: Tank off, no sparks or flames anywhere near.

steps.title: Free the plug cap
steps.instruction: Pull the spark plug cap off by its body.

steps.title: Clear the head cover
steps.instruction: Unclip the fuel pump lead from its bracket and remove the cable guide bolt.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder head cover
steps.instruction: Remove the head cover bolts and their washers and lift the cover off. Take out the head cover gasket and the spark plug hole gasket.

steps.title: Open the alternator cover
steps.instruction: Remove the two plugs or caps from the alternator cover: one shows the timing mark, the other gives access to the rotor nut.

steps.title: Set top dead centre on compression
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise with a wrench on the rotor nut until the top mark lines up with the grooves on the alternator cover. steps.title: Measure every valve
steps.instruction: Slide feeler gauges between each cam lobe and its rocker arm, for all four valves. Write down every reading.

steps.title: Compare with the standard
steps.instruction: The intake clearance must be 0.08 to 0.12 mm (0.0031 to 0.0047 in.) and the exhaust clearance 0.14 to 0.18 mm (0.0055 to 0.0071 in.).

branches.label: Any valve out of range
branches.condition: Adjusting the clearance means changing shims: have a competent mechanic do it before the engine runs again, and record the readings.

steps.title: Prepare the seals
steps.instruction: Clean any oil off the liquid gasket areas with a high flash-point solvent and dry them. Make sure the upper chain guide is bottomed against the cover, or the cam chain can lift the cover and cause a leak.
verification: New gaskets in place, chain guide bottomed.

steps.title: Refit the head cover
steps.instruction: Fit the cover, put the washers on with their metal side up and tighten the bolts to 10 N·m (89 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the alternator cover plugs
steps.instruction: Refit the two plugs or caps. Tighten them to 3.5 N·m (31 in·lb).

steps.title: Refit the plug cap
steps.instruction: Push the plug cap on in line with the mark on the head cover and pull up lightly to check it has snapped on.

steps.title: Refit the cable guide
steps.instruction: Refit the cable guide bolt (10 N·m (89 in·lb)) and clip the fuel pump lead back on its bracket.

steps.title: Refit the tank and fuel line
steps.instruction: Check the joint lock on the fuel hose for wear or bending: a bent lock means a new fuel hose. Wipe a trace of engine oil on the outlet pipe, push the hose joint straight on until it clicks, then push the lock home until it clicks. Push and pull the joint a few times to prove it is locked. Reconnect the fuel pump connector and hold the lead in its clamps. Make sure the frame dampers are in place and the throttle cables are not trapped, then set the tank down and fit the tank bolt. Tighten the bolt to 8.0 N·m (71 in·lb). Hook the band back on.

steps.title: Refit the shrouds and seat
steps.instruction: Fit both radiator shrouds. Tighten the shroud bolts to 7.0 N·m (62 in·lb). Refit the covers you removed, slide the seat forward so its hooks go under the frame collar, and fit the seat bolts. Tighten them to 25 N·m (18 ft·lb). Pull up on the back of the seat to be sure it is held.

steps.title: Run and check for leaks
steps.instruction: Start the engine, let it idle and look round the head cover for oil leaks.

steps.title: Record the readings
steps.instruction: Write down all four clearances and whether any valve needs adjusting.

title: Check the hydraulic clutch
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Clutch frees and engages properly, checked and recorded.
completeness: Covers the routine clutch check and the rider adjustments.

required_parts.name: Clutch fluid
required_parts.purpose: Fresh fluid of the grade marked on the reservoir cap, only if topping up.

critical_stop_conditions: Clutch slips or will not release: do not ride until it is put right.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the clutch after each race (or 2.5 hours) and its fluid level after each race (or 2.5 hours). The clutch fluid is changed every 2 years by someone with bleeding equipment. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Check the fluid level
steps.instruction: Turn the handlebar so the clutch reservoir sits level. The fluid must be up to the upper level line.

branches.label: Level low
branches.condition: Fluid below the upper line: look for a leak, then top up.

steps.title: Top up if needed
steps.instruction: Clean the cap, open the reservoir and fill to the upper level line with fresh fluid of the grade marked on the reservoir cap, from a sealed container. Never mix brands; if you do not know what is in there, have the whole system changed. Do not spill it on paint.
verification: Level at the upper line, cap closed.

steps.title: Check the hose and fittings
steps.instruction: Look for fluid round the master cylinder, the hose fittings and the slave cylinder, and for cracks or chafing on the hose.

steps.title: Feel the lever
steps.instruction: Pull the lever several times. It must feel firm and consistent.

branches.label: Lever soft or spongy
branches.condition: A soft or spongy lever means air in the line or a faulty clutch: do not ride, have it bled and checked, and record it.

steps.title: Set the lever position
steps.instruction: To move the lever closer or further, slide back the dust cover, loosen the locknut, turn the adjuster with a wrench, then tighten the locknut.
verification: Lever where the rider wants it, locknut tight.

steps.title: Test the clutch
steps.instruction: Start the engine and check the clutch does not slip and releases fully.

steps.title: Record the check
steps.instruction: Write down the fluid level, lever feel and anything you found.

title: Check and adjust the clutch cable
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Clutch frees and engages properly, checked and recorded.
completeness: Covers the routine clutch check and the rider adjustments.
critical_stop_conditions: Clutch slips or will not release: do not ride until it is put right.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check the clutch after each race (or 2.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Check the lever free play
steps.instruction: Pull the clutch lever gently until you feel the cable start to work the clutch. There must be a small, definite amount of free play at the lever before the clutch starts to bite. No free play makes the clutch slip; too much stops it releasing.

branches.label: Free play correct
branches.condition: Go straight to the test.

steps.title: Adjust at the lever
steps.instruction: Slide back the dust cover, loosen the locknut at the lever and turn the adjuster until the free play is right, then tighten the locknut. Make sure the top end of the outer cable is fully seated in its fitting.
verification: Free play set at the lever.

branches.label: Adjuster at its limit
branches.condition: Not enough adjustment at the lever: turn the lever adjuster fully in, lock it, and use the cable adjuster.

steps.title: Adjust at the cable if needed
steps.instruction: If the lever adjuster runs out, turn it all the way in and lock it, then loosen the locknut on the cable adjuster lower down and turn the adjusting nut until the free play is right. Tighten the locknut.

steps.title: Test the clutch
steps.instruction: Start the engine and check the clutch does not slip and releases fully, with neutral easy to find.

steps.title: Record the check
steps.instruction: Write down the free play and anything you adjusted.

title: Choose the DFI map connector
entry_state: Engine stopped.
exit_state: Chosen map connector fitted, choice recorded.
completeness: Covers swapping the track-condition map connector and confirming it took effect.
excluded: Custom maps with a calibration kit

required_parts.name: Map connectors
required_parts.purpose: White, Green and Black connectors supplied with the bike.

prerequisites: Engine stopped: a connector swapped with the engine running does not change the map.
critical_stop_conditions: Never ride with the socket open: always leave one connector fitted to keep mud out.

steps.title: Record the current map
steps.instruction: Write down which connector is fitted now and how the bike felt on the last ride.

steps.title: Stop the engine
steps.instruction: Make sure the engine is off before you touch the connector.

steps.title: Pick the map
steps.instruction: Pick the connector for the track: White for soft, slippery ground; Green for normal conditions; Black for hard-packed, high-grip tracks.

steps.title: Swap the connector
steps.instruction: Unplug the connector on the right front of the frame and plug in the one you chose until it clicks. Keep the others clean and dry.

steps.title: Start and test
steps.instruction: Start the engine and ride a test lap to feel the change.

steps.title: Record the choice
steps.instruction: Write down the connector colour, the track and how it rode.

title: Get ready to change the DFI map with the smartphone app
entry_state: Engine stopped, bike on a stand.
exit_state: Serial number and PIN recorded, bike ready to pair with the app.
completeness: Covers finding the communication unit serial number and PIN and the basic rules for changing the fuel and ignition settings with the app.

required_tools.name: Smartphone with the RIDEOLOGY THE APP KX app

critical_stop_conditions: Do not lose the PIN: write it down before refitting the covers.

steps.title: Record the current settings
steps.instruction: Write down the power mode and traction settings you use now and how the bike felt.

steps.title: Take off the air cleaner cover
steps.instruction: Pull the air cleaner cover out of its grommets and unhook its lower edge.

steps.title: Take off the left side cover
steps.instruction: Remove the seat bolt and the side cover bolt and take off the left side cover.

steps.title: Find the serial number and PIN
steps.instruction: Unplug the communication unit connector and take the unit out. Peel back its rubber cover and write down the serial number and PIN.
verification: Serial number and PIN written down.

steps.title: Refit everything
steps.instruction: Refit the communication unit and plug in its connector, then refit the side cover, seat bolt and air cleaner cover.

steps.title: Pair the app
steps.instruction: Install the app, pair it with the bike using the serial number and PIN, and change the fuel and ignition settings for each power mode as needed. The adjustable range can differ between power modes.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a test lap in each power mode you changed.

steps.title: Record the settings
steps.instruction: Write down every setting you changed and the track it was for.
